name: Emergency Response Support System (ERSS)
notes: Single emergency number for police, fire and ambulance. Women Helpline 181 and Child Helpline 1098 are linked to it, so calls can be transferred.

name: Women Helpline (Ministry of Women and Child Development)
notes: Toll-free. Refers women to police, hospitals, legal aid and One Stop Centres, and gives information on government schemes. Integrated with 112.

name: National Commission for Women (NCW) Women Helpline
notes: For women and girls above 18. Trained counsellors register complaints and refer to police, hospitals, legal services and One Stop Centres. For an emergency call 112.

name: National Commission for Women: online complaint
notes: Register a complaint online: domestic violence, dowry, harassment, rape, police refusing to register an FIR, sexual harassment at work, and more.

name: NALSA Legal Aid Helpline
notes: Toll-free free legal aid: speak to a panel lawyer. Women are entitled to free legal services regardless of income. Hindi and English.

name: National Cyber Crime Helpline and Reporting Portal
notes: Report online harassment, stalking, morphed images, sextortion and financial fraud. The portal has a special focus on cyber crimes against women and children and allows anonymous reporting of sexual content involving children.

name: Child Helpline
notes: For any child (under 18) in need of care and protection, including girls facing abuse or child marriage. Linked to 112 for emergencies.

name: SHe-Box: sexual harassment at work
notes: Online complaint for sexual harassment at the workplace, for women in any job, organised or unorganised, public or private. The complaint goes to the authority responsible.

name: Tele MANAS mental health helpline
notes: Free counselling by phone in 20 languages (Ministry of Health and Family Welfare).

name: Rail Madad: help on trains
notes: Security help for passengers in distress on trains and at stations; linked to 112. RPF "Meri Saheli" teams look after women travelling alone.
